original_test_intent: Verify that the platform rejects an approved unsupported DIMM population, records the correct DIMM/slot fault through BMC and recovered UEFI SEL, asserts the intended indicators, and returns healthy after supported memory is restored.
original_method: A qualified technician installs the documented unsupported DIMM population under powered-down ESD controls; automation observes memory-training and boot milestones via BMC, captures slot-specific faults and indicators, then verifies UEFI SEL and health after the supported layout is restored.
manual_activity: A qualified technician powers down, discharges, applies ESD controls, installs the approved unsupported DIMM population, later restores the supported layout, and observes physical indicators lacking telemetry.
required_inputs: Unsupported DIMM PN, type, rank, density and speed
Expected BMC/UEFI event IDs and slot mapping
safety_requirements: Agent never performs physical DIMM work
Use qualified technician, power discharge and ESD controls
Verify voltage, keying and form-factor safety even when unsupported
Preserve baseline logs instead of clearing them
Stop on abnormal current, heat or wrong-slot event
Do not repeatedly retrain a failing population
Verify full capacity, ECC and thermals after recovery
agent_execution_scope: Verify approved DIMM and slot plan
Guide but never perform the swap
Observe power, memory-training, POST and boot milestones
Collect BMC inventory/events and available indicator telemetry
Verify capacity, channels, ECC and health
engineer_actions: Approve unsupported and recovery DIMM populations
Define training/boot deadline and event oracle

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The narrative correctly prohibits agent-performed DIMM replacement but provides no bounded BMC inventory/event commands, training timeout, exact unsupported population or recovery checks.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Automate only read-only BMC inventory, memory-training/POST observation, event capture and post-restoration capacity/ECC health around a technician-controlled powered-down swap.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Unsupported same-type DIMMs, boot attempt, BMC web/UEFI SEL checks, lightpath/fault indicators and 20/10-minute timing are preserved; parts and slots are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a slot-population ledger with DIMM labels/SPD identity, pre/post photos, OOB memory-training timeline, event-to-slot decoding and a recovered capacity/ECC report.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes unsupported identity, rejection stage and restoration measurable while preserving technician custody.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Separates intended compatibility rejection from seating error, wrong population order, electrical fault or generic no-POST.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some unsupported modules may be electrically safe but train partially or at a fallback speed; the approved oracle must define whether that is rejection or unexpected boot.

project_override_considerations: 'Unsupported DIMMs of the same type' must name the exact unsupported attribute under the platform population rules. An arbitrary unqualified module is not a safe test vector.
expected_evidence: DIMM PN/SPD identity and documented unsupported reason
BMC inventory and exact slot events
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria consistently target an unsupported DIMM rejection. The exact unsupported attribute, topology and timeout are missing project inputs rather than contradictory requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Approved DIMMs, topology, qualified lab and recovery memory are finite inputs; execution becomes blocked only if they cannot be established after request.

review_improvement: Recovers safe automation value while preventing an arbitrary memory-training failure or seating problem from being accepted as the expected unsupported-DIMM result.
independent_technical_reasoning: Memory compatibility is population- and topology-dependent: a module can be unsupported because of rank, density, voltage, speed or firmware qualification even when physically keyed correctly. Therefore the test must bind exact SPD identity and slots and observe the training-stage rejection plus matching event. Physical handling stays manual, but OOB evidence and recovery health are automatable, so REQUIRES is appropriate.
